baseline.text: The product will be a TV remote control only.
Ambiguity about product scope: universal remote vs TV remote.
Feasibility: the proposed price around 25 EUR may be too high given production cost of 12.5 EUR.
No LCD and no speech recognition due to budget constraints.
Pursue an elderly-friendly, simple remote design with large buttons, standard conventions, top 10% of buttons on the top for reachability, and no two-level navigation.
There is a tight timeline to get the product to market.
Skip teletext option; teletext is outdated.
Lighting indicators: red LED indicator and a light under the numbers and keypad that lights briefly when a button is pressed.
Paul Wiezer (UI) will present the next item after this meeting.

The product scope was clarified as a TV remote only, addressing ambiguity between universal remote and TV remote. The team flagged feasibility concerns, noting a proposed price around 25 EUR may be high relative to a production cost of 12.5 EUR. Key design decisions were set: no LCD or speech recognition due to budget, an elderly-friendly, simple layout with large buttons, top-accessible buttons, no two-level navigation, teletext skipped, and a red LED plus a brief under-key lighting indicator. A tight market timeline was identified as a risk, with action item that Paul Wiezer will present the next item after this meeting.

gold.text: The Project Manager announced that the remote should only control television, and that the marketing should be targeted towards ages 40 and above.
The Marketing Expert presented the results of a lab study on users of remote controls, and showed that users want a fancier, less complicated remote that does not get lost easily.
The group decided not to use speech recognition or an LCD screen to target the older demographic.
The User Interface Designer discussed the button functions and how to make channel-changing easier.
The group decided not to include programmable "favorites" buttons.
The Industrial Designer presented the internal components of the device.
The group discussed having the remote light up when used.
He also stressed that the remote must be compatible with all television brands.
The Project Manager corrected his target group announcement and announced that the target age group was actually ages 40 and below.
The group again discussed the possibility of adding speech recognition and LCD screens to the design but decided that it was not feasible.
The group decided to have the remote light up when used and is including teletext.
The Marketing Expert was instructed to report on trendwatching.
The Marketing Expert will prepare a report on trendwatching.
The remote will not feature speech recognition or an LCD screen.
The remote will light up when a button is pressed, much like a mobile phone.
Basic buttons will go on top and other buttons lower down, all on a single level.
The remote will feature teletext capabilities, and the teletext buttons will be included on the main interface.
There was a misunderstanding about the target user group that forced the group to reevaluate their decisions on several components once they received the correct information.
The new requirement that the remote was only to control television forced the group to change some of their initial design ideas.
The group did not reach a decision on how to ensure that the remote would recognize all brands of televisions.
The remote will use an automatic search function to find the code for the user's television brand.
The remote will not have programmable favourites buttons.
The remote will control only the television, replacing the earlier universal-remote decision.
